title: Canonical docs contradict the implementation on the ATTACH draw domain (district-scoped vs global ring)
evidence: core/map.odin:33-36: "board: the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's OWN district's pool (an // estate never crosses a district boundary), and the derived cluster view is // unchanged (radius adjacency) — the district scoping at the DRAW makes // cross-district estates unreachable by construction." — but core/growth.odin:532: "caller draws one index. The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped): the" and the implementation core/growth.odin:541-547 has no district filter: "for k in 0..<len(board.candidates) { // c := board.candidates[k] // d := c - anchor // d2 := i64(d[0]) * i64(d[0]) + i64(d[1]) * i64(d[1]) // if d2 >= lo2 && d2 <= hi2 { // append(ring, u32(k))". demos/dublin_board.dem:5-7 repeats the false claim: "the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's # district pool — a cluster never crosses a district boundary)." and core/map_test.odin:13: "family stays WITHIN the anchor's district (the growth_groups" while the test body never checks district containment.
detail: Three committed documents (core loader header, the blessed demo's header, the test header) state a district-scoped ATTACH contract the code does not implement. Future stage-2 work following map.odin would change replay-relevant spawn behavior.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the map.odin district paragraph, dublin_board.dem header, and map_test.odin comment (d) to describe the global street ring (the growth.odin text is the accurate one).

title: The '1-in-6 snap/dedupe/grid-filter' unit pin only exercises stride+snap — dedupe and grid-filter paths are never tested
evidence: core/map_test.odin:109: "src := `{\"board\":{\"w_tiles\":8,\"h_tiles\":6},\"spawn_candidates\":[[1.1,1.2],[1.3,1.4],[1.5,1.6],[7.9,5.1],[-0.4,2.0],[2.0,6.4]],...}`" with MAP_SPAWN_STRIDE :: 6 (core/map.odin:63) — stride-6 over 6 candidates samples index 0 only, so the out-of-grid points at indices 3-5 are never sampled and one point cannot dedupe. The test itself says: "// stride 6 over 6 candidates = 1 point (the first). It snaps to (1,1)." and asserts only "testing.expectf(t, len(b.candidates) == 1, ..." and "testing.expectf(t, b.candidates[0] == [2]i32{1, 1}, ..." while its header claims "(a) stride -> snap -> grid filter -> dedupe: the pool holds integer // TILES only, in first-occurrence order; out-of-grid points never enter."
detail: The PR-claimed pin for briefing rule 3 (filter at bake-load: grid-filter + dedupe) passes without testing either path. A regression in the loader's filter/dedupe logic would go undetected.
recommended_fix: Extend the fixture (e.g. 12+ candidates so stride-6 samples an out-of-grid point and two points snapping to the same tile) and assert the filtered/deduped pool shape.

title: District pool data and helpers ship in core with no sim-path consumer
evidence: core/map.odin:446-450: "// map_board_candidate_pool — the global pool range (the SEED family's draw // domain): ... // map_board_pool_lo :: proc(b: ^Map_Board) -> u32 { return 0 } // map_board_pool_hi :: proc(b: ^Map_Board) -> u32 { return u32(len(b.candidates)) }" — grep across core/ app/ harness/ demos/ shows map_board_pool_lo/hi have zero call sites. The district_start prefix-sum (map.odin:390-404: "b.district_start = make([dynamic]u32, len(b.districts) + 1, allocator) ... acc += counts[di]") and board_district_at (core/growth.odin:501) are referenced only by core/map_test.odin:42 ("append(&b.candidate_district, board_district_at(&b, b.candidates[i]))"), never by growth's draw path.
detail: Loaded, indexed, and helper-wrapped data retained for a hypothetical future policy is premature surface; combined with the contradictory district docs it actively misleads maintainers about the live behavior.
recommended_fix: Either wire district_start/candidate_district into the draw or trim them (plus the lo/hi helpers) until the district-scoped policy actually lands.

title: growth_board_ring_scan declares unused `t: ^Topology` and `alloc` parameters
evidence: core/growth.odin:537: "growth_board_ring_scan :: proc(board: ^Map_Board, t: ^Topology, anchor: [2]i32, sep, radius: i32, ring: ^[dynamic]u32, alloc := context.temp_allocator) -> i32 {" — the body references neither: "lo2 := i64(sep) * i64(sep) // hi2 := i64(radius) * i64(radius) // clear(ring) // for k in 0..<len(board.candidates) { // c := board.candidates[k] // d := c - anchor // d2 := i64(d[0]) * i64(d[0]) + i64(d[1]) * i64(d[1]) // if d2 >= lo2 && d2 <= hi2 { // append(ring, u32(k))"
detail: Dead parameters imply a topology dependence the scan does not have, and the unused `alloc` bypasses the explicit-allocator intent (appends fall back to the ring's implicit allocator) — ODN-18 hygiene noise.
recommended_fix: Drop `t` and `alloc` from the signature (append reuses the caller's scratch buffer), or thread `alloc` into append explicitly.

title: map_board_load leaks partial board allocations on its fail-loud error paths
evidence: core/map.odin:319: "append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})" — after which later failures return without freeing b's buffers, e.g. map.odin:322-323: "if len(b.districts) == 0 { // return {}, \"map_board_load: no districts\"" and the terrain/street failures at lines 410-422 return after candidates/districts are built. The only defers are `defer json.destroy_value(v, allocator)` and `defer delete(snapped)`; there is no `defer map_board_destroy(&b)` on error.
detail: A corrupt-asset load discards the partially built Map_Board's dynamic arrays. Under the project's own ODN-18 tracking-allocator rule this is a leak on the fallback-to-procedural path.
recommended_fix: On each error return after allocations begin, call map_board_destroy(&b) (or one deferred destroy guarded by the err result) before returning.

title: dublin.odin hand-rolls cstring copies where the package already uses strings.clone_to_cstring
evidence: app/render/dublin.odin:385: "w := rl.MeasureTextEx(v.font, cstring(raw_data(dublin_label_cstr(d.name))), f32(size), 1)" then :387: "draw_text_font_halo(v.font, d.name, i32(x), i32(y), size, ink, halo)" — draw_text_font_halo (line 405) rebuilds the copy internally: "cbuf := make([dynamic]u8, 0, len(txt) + 1, context.temp_allocator) // for b in transmute([]u8)(txt) { // append(&cbuf, b) // }". The package's existing helper noc_overlay.odin:516-519: "strings_clone_cstr_noc :: proc(s: string, v: ^View) -> cstring { // return strings.clone_to_cstring(s, context.temp_allocator) // }".
detail: Two conventions for the same temp-cstring need now coexist in one package, and each label pays a duplicate per-frame copy (measure + draw) versus the one-line stdlib call.
recommended_fix: Replace dublin_label_cstr and the inline loops with strings.clone_to_cstring(s, context.temp_allocator) (matching noc_overlay), and pass the measured cstring through to the draw.

title: board_cache/board_cache_loaded introduce the first file-scope mutable state in the harness
evidence: harness/catalogs.odin:85-86: "board_cache: pp.Map_Board // board_cache_loaded: bool" — a grep for file-scope value declarations across harness/*.odin finds no other package-level mutable state; every other harness dependency (catalogs, Render_Ctx, demo config) is threaded by parameter. board_load mutates it: "board_cache = b // board_cache_loaded = true // return &board_cache, \"\"".
detail: The harness was uniformly stateless-per-verb; a mutable package cache breaks that precedent and would silently misbehave if a verb ever reloaded a different board in one process.
recommended_fix: Load the board once in main() per verb invocation (the load_catalogs pattern) and pass ^pp.Map_Board down alongside cat, keeping the process stateless.
